root_cause: An exit-condition invariant in dbRandomKey() ('the only way expireIfNeeded() can refuse to delete an expired key without eventually returning 0 is if this is a replica') was silently broken when a second such path (client-pause-driven expire suppression on a primary) was introduced elsewhere, without the dbRandomKey() guard being updated to match the new invariant.
findings: dbRandomKey() retries dictGetFairRandomKey() in a while(1) loop whenever the randomly-picked key is volatile and logically expired, relying on expireIfNeeded() to either actually delete the key (allowing the loop to terminate on a non-expired pick) or on a maxtries safety valve to force termination when the DB cannot make progress.
